perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- Christian knows he is a police officer and that Jonathan Balogun is his best friend since childhood. He often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- He noticed Jonathan acting differently and felt Jonathan was hiding something important. This made him anxious and suspicious.
- He arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop and confronted Jonathan.
- Christian heard Jonathan admit he had been keeping something from him: Jonathan is in some kind of trouble and did not know how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic and offered his help and support. He heard Jonathan say the situation is complicated, that he does not want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support and resources and needs to get out of a mess.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might be related to criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. He heard Jonathan say he could not be sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he would look into the matter discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian found/believed Jonathan was being framed—someone was trying to set him up. Christian told Jonathan he had leads but did not yet know who was responsible, and decided to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Later, Christian came to believe he had identified the real culprit as someone close to both him and Jonathan. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it and that it was someone they both know and trust.
- Christian felt betrayed and resolute and decided to confront the real culprit and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him the person is dangerous and expressed trust in him.
- The supplied text does not name the culprit, but Christian states that he knows who it is.
